title: How Good Are Frontier Models at Physics? Expert Re-Grading Reveals Broken Evaluations and Near-Saturation of Leading Benchmarks
note: arXiv:2609.13009v1, submitted 11 Sep 2026, CC BY 4.0. Not peer reviewed. 51 authors; 39 data auditors performed the audits, 12 physics advisors did not (Appendix G). Corresponding author John Sous (Yale). Funded by Yale Office of the Provost AI Initiatives and a Jump Trading Group gift.

title: Humanity's Last Exam
note: arXiv:2501.14249. Abstract claims answers are "unambiguous and easily verifiable"; §3.2 states reviewers were not expected to verify full solution accuracy if it would take more than five minutes, and invites community feedback.

title: Probing the Critical Point (CritPt) of AI Reasoning
note: arXiv:2509.26574. States every problem is hand-curated to admit a guess-resistant, machine-verifiable answer; over 40 hours of expert effort per problem.

title: CMT-Benchmark
note: arXiv:2510.05228. States the dataset was designed and verified by a panel of expert researchers.

title: PHYBench: Holistic Evaluation of Physical Perception and Reasoning in Large Language Models
note: arXiv:2504.16074. Source of the Expression Edit Distance (EED) metric and the +204% sample efficiency claim over binary scoring.

title: PRISM-Physics: Causal DAG-Based Process Evaluation for Physics Reasoning
note: arXiv:2510.03185. Not to be confused with arXiv:2512.05930 "PRiSM", a different paper. Claims fully rule-based symbolic equivalence matching ensuring consistent validation without heuristic judging.

title: UGPhysics: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Undergraduate Physics Reasoning with Large Language Models
note: arXiv:2502.00334. Claims rigorous screening for data leakage and a Model-Assistant Rule-based Judgment pipeline ensuring accurate evaluation.

title: Pervasive Label Errors in Test Sets Destabilize Machine Learning Benchmarks
note: arXiv:2103.14749. ImageNet validation label error rate 5.83% (2,916 of 50,000). Re-ranking on the error-containing subset moves NASNet-large from 1st to 29th and ResNet-18 from 34th to 1st. Denominator is the full test set, unlike the 250 audited rejections in this report.

title: Claude Fable 5.1 & Claude Mythos 5.1 System Card
note: §8.9 CritPt-Corrected. Source PDF could not be opened directly; the description in this report is routed through Appendix B.2.3 of ansari2026physics and public secondary summaries. 31 of 71 problem statements expert-revised; mean@16 with tools, Claude Opus 4.8 as judge, 88.4%.

title: Intelligence Index Methodology
note: CritPt leaderboard value (GPT-5.6-Sol Max 32.3%) checked 15 Sep 2026. No published methodology for validating reference answers or grader reliability was found.

title: What Will it Take to Fix Benchmarking in Natural Language Understanding?
note: Cited through the summary in §4 of ansari2026physics; the original text was not consulted for this report.

title: JudgeBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLM-Based Judges
note: arXiv:2410.12784. One of the few studies that benchmarks judge accuracy against objective ground truth.

title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
note: arXiv:2306.05685. Reports judge-human agreement rather than absolute judge error rate, which is the pattern described in §5.3 of this report.

title: AI Index Report 2026
note: Background for the claim that benchmark lifespans have shortened to months.
